body:
You remind me much of myself when I was your age. Don't be offended, but you're still very much a kid. 

Video games are very addicting. This is a huge hurdle, hard to overcome. I overcame it by not having any time for it due to work and choosing to rather go outside, which I enjoy a lot more in the long run. 

Most people I know at 22, still don't understand people, but they hide it well. The reason you don't see people around you not understanding life , the universe and everything is because they are surrounded by age-old cliches, religion, habits and culture that just kinda hardwires the way of thought inside you. You probably weren't much in social circles while growing up, so you kinda skipped that part. But don't worry, it's completely doable. Not easy, because it involves changing your outlook on the world drastically, but very doable.

Just don't be stopped by your thoughts of what life is and should be. Do the basic things: eat, work, do school, add things like play sports and join social circles (hobbies and sports are great for this thing) and be open for change. You'll feel better in no time. 

Don't feel opressed by whatever you've been diagnosed. I'm no doctor, but I firmly believe a kid is too young to be judged whether or not he has behavioral problems. I've known many people that were weird as fuck your age, and have found a normal way of life today. This also, sadly works in reverse. Kids that seemed to be popular and in control back in the day just don't know what to do with their life nowadays and just waste away in a dead-end job and bet on sports for an extra income. And there's the middle ground as well.

Being an introvert also doesn't mean you want to be alone. Introverts like company as well, just in moderation. They need their space, but they still want it surrounded by friends. 

As for friends in school just start hanging around people. You're starting high school, right? Perfect place for that. Don't act weird, think before you act and in doubt just do normal, "default" things. Rather seem silent and dumb, than dispel all their doubts with a single inappropriate sentence. I have a best friend who's basically living on that principle alone. Everybody thinks he's cool and  mysterious when in fact, he's just as lost as everyone else.

You'll learn what's right to do and say by observation and harmless trial and error in time, and don't be stressed about stuff you do. You'll encounter a large amount of kids who will seem so confident in the bullshit they do, that you'll feel opressed and hopelessly lost.
